IM-1.t: Trace thymic development from third pharyngeal pouch endoderm (shared with the inferior parathyroids), with neural crest derived capsule and septa, and its descent into the anterior mediastinum.
Describe colonization of the thymic epithelial framework by bone marrow derived T cell precursors and the formation of cortex, medulla, and Hassall corpuscles during fetal life.

Relate failed third and fourth pharyngeal pouch development in 22q11.2 deletion (DiGeorge) syndrome to absent thymic shadow, T cell deficiency, hypocalcemia from parathyroid hypoplasia or aplasia, and conotruncal heart defects.
IM-1.usmle: Immune System: Disorders associated with immunodeficiency: primarily cell-mediated deficiency: DiGeorge syndrome

IM-1.t: Describe age-related thymic involution with replacement by adipose tissue, and explain why established peripheral T cell immunity persists after involution or adult thymectomy.

Locate the adult thymus in the anterior and superior mediastinum behind the manubrium, and distinguish thymoma from the other classic anterior mediastinal masses (teratoma, lymphoma, retrosternal thyroid).

IM-2.t: Describe lymph node microanatomy: capsule and subcapsular sinus, cortical B cell follicles with germinal centers, paracortical T cells with high endothelial venules, and medullary cords and sinuses.

Predict which lymph node zone is depleted in DiGeorge syndrome (paracortex) and X-linked agammaglobulinemia (follicles and germinal centers), and which expands in reactive follicular versus paracortical hyperplasia.
IM-2.usmle: Immune System: Disorders associated with immunodeficiency

IM-2.t: Describe splenic histology: white pulp (periarteriolar lymphoid sheath of T cells, B cell follicles, marginal zone) and red pulp (cords of Billroth and venous sinusoids), and trace blood flow through them.
Distinguish thymic cortex (densely packed immature thymocytes, epithelial reticular cells, blood thymus barrier) from medulla (mature T cells, Hassall corpuscles) on a histologic section.
Describe mucosa associated lymphoid tissue, including tonsils and ileal Peyer patches with antigen-sampling M cells, and explain its role in generating IgA-secreting plasma cells.

IM-3.t: Compare MHC class I (HLA-A, -B, -C; heavy chain with beta2-microglobulin; all nucleated cells; presents to CD8 T cells) with class II (HLA-DP, -DQ, -DR; antigen-presenting cells; presents to CD4 T cells).
Trace antigen processing for class I (proteasome, TAP transport, loading in the endoplasmic reticulum) and class II (endosomal degradation, invariant chain, CLIP exchange by HLA-DM).
Describe the HLA locus on chromosome 6, codominant expression, polymorphism, and haplotype inheritance, and calculate the probability (25%) that a sibling is a full HLA match for transplantation.
IM-3.usmle: Immune System: Immunologically mediated disorders: transplantation

IM-3.t: Relate HLA alleles to disease: B27 (ankylosing spondylitis, reactive and psoriatic arthritis), DQ2 and DQ8 (celiac disease), DR3 and DR4 (type 1 diabetes), DR4 (rheumatoid arthritis), and DR2 (multiple sclerosis, Goodpasture syndrome).
Explain how NK cells kill cells that lose MHC class I expression (missing self), and why virus-infected and tumor cells that downregulate class I become NK targets.
Explain how preformed anti-HLA antibodies from prior transfusion, pregnancy, or transplant cause hyperacute rejection, and why crossmatching and HLA matching improve graft survival.
IM-3.usmle: Immune System: Immunologically mediated disorders: transplantation

IM-4.t: Trace lymph from the lower limbs, pelvis, and abdomen through the cisterna chyli and thoracic duct to the left venous angle, and contrast the right lymphatic duct territory (right head, neck, upper limb, thorax).
Identify the regions drained by the palpable node groups (cervical, supraclavicular, axillary, epitrochlear, superficial inguinal) and predict which group enlarges with an infection of a given site.

Predict first nodal spread of tumors: lateral breast to axillary and medial breast to parasternal nodes, testis to para-aortic but scrotum to superficial inguinal nodes, and anal canal above the pectinate line to internal iliac but below it to superficial inguinal nodes.
Relate an enlarged left supraclavicular (Virchow) node to abdominal or thoracic malignancy spreading along the thoracic duct.
Predict chylothorax after thoracic duct injury and describe the milky, triglyceride-rich pleural fluid containing chylomicrons and lymphocytes.

IM-5.t: Describe immunoglobulin structure (two heavy and two light chains, Fab with hypervariable antigen-binding regions, Fc determining isotype functions such as complement fixation and Fc receptor binding).

Compare the isotypes: IgM (pentamer, first response, strongest complement activation), IgG (placental transfer, opsonization), secretory IgA (mucosal dimer), IgE (mast cells, helminths), and IgD (naive B cell receptor).

Explain T cell dependent B cell activation, including CD40L to CD40 signaling and cytokines driving isotype switching and affinity maturation in germinal centers, and contrast T independent responses to polysaccharide antigens.
IM-5.usmle: Immune System: Disorders associated with immunodeficiency: primarily humoral deficiency: hyper-IgM syndrome

IM-5.t: Compare Th1 (IL-12 induced; IFN-gamma activates macrophages), Th2 (IL-4, IL-5, IL-13; IgE and eosinophils), Th17 (IL-17; neutrophils against extracellular bacteria and fungi), and regulatory T cells (FOXP3; IL-10, TGF-beta).
Explain how CD8 cytotoxic T cells and NK cells kill target cells through perforin and granzymes and through Fas ligand binding Fas, both producing apoptosis.
Interpret primary versus secondary antibody response curves (lag phase, IgM then IgG, higher titer and affinity on re-exposure), and distinguish active from passive immunity such as maternal IgG.

IM-6.t: Describe pattern recognition: TLR4 with CD14 binding LPS, TLR5 binding flagellin, endosomal TLR3, 7, 8, and 9 binding nucleic acids, and the NLRP3 inflammasome activating caspase-1 to release IL-1beta in response to DAMPs.

Trace leukocyte extravasation (selectin rolling, integrin adhesion to ICAM-1 induced by TNF and IL-1, PECAM-1 diapedesis, chemotaxis to C5a, LTB4, IL-8) and relate CD18 deficiency to leukocyte adhesion deficiency.
IM-6.usmle: Immune System: Disorders associated with immunodeficiency: phagocyte and NK cell deficiencies: leukocyte adhesion deficiency

IM-6.t: Explain the acute phase response: IL-1, IL-6, and TNF-alpha cause fever through hypothalamic PGE2, raise CRP, fibrinogen, serum amyloid A, ferritin, and hepcidin, and lower albumin and transferrin.
Explain opsonization by IgG and C3b and phagolysosome fusion, and relate LYST mutation in Chediak-Higashi syndrome to giant granules, partial albinism, neuropathy, and recurrent pyogenic infections.
IM-6.usmle: Immune System: Disorders associated with immunodeficiency: phagocyte and NK cell deficiencies: Chediak-Higashi disease

IM-6.t: Describe the foreign body granuloma (macrophages, epithelioid cells, foreign body giant cells around sutures, talc, or splinters) and distinguish it from an immune granuloma driven by Th1 IFN-gamma.

Explain how LPS signaling through TLR4 drives TNF, IL-1, and IL-6 release in sepsis, causing vasodilation, capillary leak, DIC, and organ dysfunction, and apply SIRS criteria (temperature above 38 °C (100.4 °F) or below 36 °C (96.8 °F), pulse, respirations, WBC).
IM-6.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Shock: sepsis and SIRS

IM-6.t: Explain how superantigens (S aureus TSST-1, S pyogenes pyrogenic exotoxins) bind MHC class II and TCR V-beta outside the peptide groove, causing polyclonal T cell activation and cytokine storm in toxic shock syndrome.
IM-6.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: bacterial infections: toxic shock syndrome

IM-7.t: Compare activation of the classical (C1q binding IgM or IgG complexes), lectin (mannose-binding lectin on microbial sugars), and alternative (spontaneous C3 hydrolysis on microbial surfaces) pathways converging on C3 convertase.
IM-7.usmle: Immune System: Disorders associated with immunodeficiency: complement deficiencies

IM-7.t: Describe complement effector functions: C3b opsonization, C3a and C5a anaphylatoxins, C5a neutrophil chemotaxis, C5b-9 membrane attack complex lysis, and clearance of immune complexes.

Explain regulation by C1 esterase inhibitor, DAF (CD55), and CD59, and predict hereditary angioedema (bradykinin-mediated swelling without urticaria, low C4) and paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PIGA mutation, intravascular hemolysis).
IM-7.usmle: Immune System: Disorders associated with immunodeficiency: complement deficiencies: C1 esterase inhibitor deficiency

IM-7.t: Predict the disease from each deficiency: C1q, C2, or C4 (SLE-like immune complex disease), C3 (severe pyogenic infections, immune complex glomerulonephritis), C5 to C9 (recurrent Neisseria), and MBL (childhood infections).
IM-7.usmle: Immune System: Disorders associated with immunodeficiency: complement deficiencies

IM-7.t: Interpret serum complement: low C3 and C4 in active SLE, low C3 with normal C4 in poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis, and low C4 with normal C3 in hereditary angioedema.
IM-7.usmle: Immune System: Immunologically mediated disorders: hypersensitivity

IM-8.t: Explain thymic T cell maturation: double negative to double positive thymocytes, positive selection on cortical epithelial MHC, and negative selection in the medulla by AIRE-driven expression of tissue antigens.
Explain splenic functions: removal of aged RBCs and inclusions, clearance of opsonized and encapsulated bacteria by marginal zone B cells and macrophages, IgM production, and platelet storage.

Predict findings after splenectomy or functional asplenia (sickle cell disease): Howell-Jolly bodies, target cells, thrombocytosis, and sepsis from S pneumoniae, H influenzae type b, and N meningitidis.
Explain naive lymphocyte homing into lymph nodes through high endothelial venules (L-selectin, CCR7), meeting antigen carried by dendritic cells in afferent lymph, and exit through efferent lymph.
Predict the effect of high cortisol (stress or Cushing syndrome) on the blood count and lymphoid organs: lymphopenia, eosinopenia, neutrophilia from demargination, and thymic atrophy.

IM-9.t: Explain lymph formation from net capillary filtration by Starling forces, with about 2 to 3 L of lymph returned to the blood each day.

Describe lymph composition (interstitial fluid with filtered plasma protein, lymphocytes, and chylomicrons in intestinal chyle) and explain why lymph is the only route returning filtered protein to the blood.

Explain lymph propulsion by intrinsic lymphangion smooth muscle contraction, one-way valves, skeletal muscle pumping, and respiratory pressure changes, and why rising interstitial pressure increases lymph flow.

Predict lymphedema (protein-rich edema that becomes nonpitting with fibrosis) from axillary dissection or radiation, Wuchereria bancrofti filariasis, Milroy disease (FLT4), and Turner syndrome (cystic hygroma).

IM-10.t: Trace the respiratory burst (NADPH from the pentose phosphate pathway, NADPH oxidase to superoxide, superoxide dismutase to H2O2, myeloperoxidase to HOCl) and relate NADPH oxidase defects to chronic granulomatous disease.
IM-10.usmle: Immune System: Disorders associated with immunodeficiency: phagocyte and NK cell deficiencies: chronic granulomatous disease

IM-10.t: Predict chronic granulomatous disease infections with catalase-positive organisms (S aureus, Aspergillus, Burkholderia cepacia, Serratia, Nocardia) and interpret an abnormal dihydrorhodamine or nitroblue tetrazolium test.
IM-10.usmle: Immune System: Disorders associated with immunodeficiency: phagocyte and NK cell deficiencies: chronic granulomatous disease

IM-10.t: Explain how adenosine deaminase deficiency causes dATP accumulation that inhibits ribonucleotide reductase and kills lymphocytes, producing autosomal recessive SCID.
IM-10.usmle: Immune System: Disorders associated with immunodeficiency: primarily cell-mediated deficiency: adenosine deaminase deficiency

IM-10.t: Compare arachidonic acid products: COX-derived PGE2 (fever, pain, vasodilation) and thromboxane, and 5-lipoxygenase-derived LTB4 (neutrophil chemotaxis) and LTC4, LTD4, LTE4 (bronchoconstriction, vascular permeability).
Explain how granuloma macrophages in sarcoidosis express 1-alpha-hydroxylase, producing calcitriol and hypercalcemia, and how vitamin D induces macrophage cathelicidin.
IM-10.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: immunologic and inflammatory disorders: sarcoidosis

IM-10.t: Relate zinc deficiency (thymic atrophy, impaired T cell function, acrodermatitis enteropathica) and vitamin A deficiency (mucosal squamous metaplasia, more severe measles) to infection risk.
Explain why protein-energy malnutrition (marasmus, kwashiorkor) is the most common cause of acquired immunodeficiency worldwide, with thymic atrophy and impaired cell-mediated immunity.

IM-11.t: Explain chylomicron assembly in enterocytes (triglyceride resynthesis, apoB-48, microsomal triglyceride transfer protein) and their entry into lacteals and thoracic duct lymph, bypassing the liver.
Trace chylomicron breakdown after entering the blood: apoC-II activation of endothelial lipoprotein lipase, fatty acid release to muscle and adipose tissue, and apoE-mediated hepatic remnant uptake.
Predict the findings of abetalipoproteinemia (MTP deficiency): absent chylomicrons and apoB lipoproteins, fat malabsorption, acanthocytes, and fat-soluble vitamin deficiency.
Explain why hepatic and intestinal lymph carry more protein than lymph from skeletal muscle, relating it to sinusoidal and fenestrated versus continuous capillary endothelium.

IM-12.t: Explain V(D)J recombination by RAG1 and RAG2 and junctional diversity from TdT, and predict that RAG deficiency causes SCID with absent T and B cells but preserved NK cells.
IM-12.usmle: Immune System: Disorders associated with immunodeficiency: primarily cell-mediated deficiency: severe combined immunodeficiency

IM-12.t: Classify SCID genotypes by lymphocyte profile: X-linked IL2RG common gamma chain (T and NK absent, B present), ADA deficiency (all absent), and RAG deficiency, with low T cell receptor excision circles.
IM-12.usmle: Immune System: Disorders associated with immunodeficiency: primarily cell-mediated deficiency: severe combined immunodeficiency

IM-12.t: Relate X-linked WAS gene mutation in Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome to thrombocytopenia with small platelets, eczema, recurrent infections, low IgM with high IgA and IgE, and calculate risk for sons of carriers.
IM-12.usmle: Immune System: Disorders associated with immunodeficiency: primarily cell-mediated deficiency: Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome

IM-12.t: Explain how X-linked CD40 ligand deficiency blocks isotype switching, producing hyper-IgM syndrome with normal or high IgM, low IgG, IgA, and IgE, and Pneumocystis and Cryptosporidium infections.
IM-12.usmle: Immune System: Disorders associated with immunodeficiency: primarily humoral deficiency: hyper-IgM syndrome

IM-12.t: Relate AIRE mutation to autoimmune polyglandular syndrome type 1 (chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis, hypoparathyroidism, adrenal insufficiency) and FOXP3 mutation to IPEX syndrome.
IM-12.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: immunologic and inflammatory disorders: polyglandular autoimmune syndrome, type 1

IM-12.t: Explain how Fas-mediated apoptosis ends lymphocyte clonal expansion and removes self-reactive lymphocytes, and predict lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly, and autoimmune cytopenias in autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome from FAS mutation.

IM-13.t: Compare innate immunity (germline pattern recognition receptors, rapid, no memory; neutrophils, macrophages, NK cells, complement) with adaptive immunity (rearranged receptors, clonal expansion, memory).
Explain two-signal T cell activation (TCR binding peptide on MHC plus CD28 binding B7), anergy when costimulation is absent, and inhibition through CTLA-4 and PD-1.
Explain antitumor immunity by CD8 T cells recognizing tumor antigens on MHC class I and by NK cells, and tumor escape through loss of MHC class I and PD-L1 expression.

Compare live attenuated vaccines (MMR, varicella, yellow fever; strong cellular and humoral immunity, avoided in immunodeficiency) with inactivated, subunit, toxoid, and protein-conjugated polysaccharide vaccines.

Explain mechanisms of autoimmunity: failed central or peripheral tolerance, HLA susceptibility, and molecular mimicry (group A strep M protein in rheumatic fever, Campylobacter jejuni in Guillain-Barre syndrome).
IM-13.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: immunologic and inflammatory disorders: acute rheumatic fever

IM-13.t: Compare the four hypersensitivity types by effector (IgE and mast cells; IgG or IgM against cell or matrix antigens; immune complexes; T cells) and time course, and classify a clinical reaction.
IM-13.usmle: Immune System: Immunologically mediated disorders: hypersensitivity

IM-14.t: Describe parvovirus B19 (small nonenveloped ssDNA virus) tropism for erythroid progenitors through the P antigen, respiratory and transplacental spread, and why infection halts red cell production.
IM-14.usmle: Skin & Subcutaneous Tissue: Infectious disorders and infestations: viral: parvovirus

IM-14.t: Describe Haemophilus influenzae type b: gram-negative coccobacillus, polyribosylribitol phosphate capsule as the key virulence factor, IgA protease, respiratory spread, and growth requiring factors X and V on chocolate agar.
IM-14.usmle: Respiratory System: Infectious disorders of the lower airways: pneumonia: Haemophilus influenzae

IM-14.t: Describe influenza virus (orthomyxovirus with segmented negative-sense RNA, hemagglutinin binding sialic acid, neuraminidase releasing virions) and distinguish antigenic drift (point mutations) from shift (reassortment causing pandemics).
IM-14.usmle: Respiratory System: Infectious disorders of the upper airways: viral infections: influenza virus

IM-14.t: Describe measles and mumps viruses (enveloped nonsegmented negative-sense RNA paramyxoviruses whose F protein forms syncytia, such as Warthin-Finkeldey cells in measles) and rubella virus (enveloped positive-sense RNA, formerly classed as a togavirus), all spread by respiratory droplets.
IM-14.usmle: Skin & Subcutaneous Tissue: Infectious disorders and infestations: viral: measles, rubella

IM-14.t: Describe the herpesviruses behind mononucleosis and roseola (enveloped dsDNA with lifelong latency): EBV entering B cells through CD21, and HHV-6 and HHV-7 infecting CD4 T cells, all spread by saliva.
IM-14.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: viral infections: infectious mononucleosis (Epstein-Barr virus)

IM-14.t: Describe Streptococcus pyogenes (catalase-negative, beta-hemolytic, bacitracin-sensitive gram-positive cocci in chains), M protein as antiphagocytic and mimicry antigen, and pyrogenic exotoxins as superantigens causing scarlet fever.
IM-14.usmle: Skin & Subcutaneous Tissue: Infectious disorders and infestations: bacterial: scarlet fever (group A Streptococcus)

IM-14.t: Trace the Toxoplasma gondii life cycle: sexual stage in the cat (definitive host), oocysts in cat feces, tissue cysts with bradyzoites in undercooked meat, and transplacental tachyzoites.
IM-14.usmle: Nervous System & Special Senses: Infectious disorders: encephalitis: Toxoplasma gondii

IM-15-A.t: Explain common variable immunodeficiency (failed B cell differentiation into plasma cells with usually normal B cell counts), its frequent onset in adulthood, low IgG and IgA, sinopulmonary and Giardia infections, and autoimmune and lymphoma risk.
IM-15-A.usmle: Immune System: Disorders associated with immunodeficiency: primarily humoral deficiency: common variable immunodeficiency

IM-15-A.t: Identify DiGeorge syndrome (22q11.2 deletion, TBX1) by cardiac defects (truncus arteriosus, tetralogy of Fallot), abnormal facies, thymic hypoplasia with viral and fungal infections, cleft palate, and hypocalcemic tetany.
IM-15-A.usmle: Immune System: Disorders associated with immunodeficiency: primarily cell-mediated deficiency: DiGeorge syndrome

IM-15-A.t: Describe selective IgA deficiency, the most common primary immunodeficiency: often asymptomatic, sinopulmonary and Giardia infections, celiac and autoimmune associations, anaphylaxis to IgA-containing blood products, and falsely negative IgA serologies.
IM-15-A.usmle: Immune System: Disorders associated with immunodeficiency: primarily humoral deficiency: selective IgA deficiency

IM-15-A.t: Identify SCID in an infant with failure to thrive, chronic diarrhea, thrush, Pneumocystis pneumonia, and severe viral infections, with absent thymic shadow, and predict harm from live vaccines and nonirradiated transfusions.
IM-15-A.usmle: Immune System: Disorders associated with immunodeficiency: primarily cell-mediated deficiency: severe combined immunodeficiency

IM-15-A.t: Explain how BTK mutation in X-linked agammaglobulinemia blocks pre-B cell maturation, leaving absent B cells, very low immunoglobulins, scant tonsils, and infections after 6 months with encapsulated bacteria, enteroviruses, and Giardia.
IM-15-A.usmle: Immune System: Disorders associated with immunodeficiency: primarily humoral deficiency: X-linked agammaglobulinemia

IM-15-A.t: Predict the defective arm from the infection pattern: B cell (encapsulated bacteria, enteroviruses), T cell (viruses, fungi, Pneumocystis), phagocyte (S aureus, Aspergillus), terminal complement (Neisseria), and choose the first test (immunoglobulin levels, flow cytometry, DHR, CH50).
IM-15-A.usmle: Immune System: Disorders associated with immunodeficiency

IM-15-B.t: Predict the infections caused by drug-induced immunodeficiency: glucocorticoids and calcineurin inhibitors (T cell suppression, Pneumocystis), TNF-alpha inhibitors (latent tuberculosis reactivation), rituximab (B cell depletion, hepatitis B reactivation), and chemotherapy neutropenia.
IM-15-B.usmle: Immune System: Adverse effects of drugs on the immune system: immunosuppressive and immune-modulating drugs

IM-15-B.t: Describe HIV structure and entry: retrovirus with gag (p24 capsid), pol (reverse transcriptase, integrase, protease), and env (gp120 binding CD4 with CCR5 or CXCR4, gp41 fusion), and why CCR5 delta32 homozygotes resist infection.
IM-15-B.usmle: Immune System: HIV/AIDS: HIV-1 and HIV-2

IM-15-B.t: Trace the natural history of HIV: transmission routes, acute retroviral syndrome, clinical latency with ongoing lymphoid replication, CD4 decline, and AIDS defined by CD4 below 200 cells per mm3 or an AIDS-defining illness.
IM-15-B.usmle: Immune System: HIV/AIDS: immunology of AIDS

IM-15-B.t: Interpret HIV testing: fourth generation antigen and antibody immunoassay followed by HIV-1 and HIV-2 differentiation, CD4 count for staging, viral load for replication, and why infants of infected mothers need nucleic acid testing rather than antibody tests.

Predict opportunistic infections by CD4 count: oral thrush and oral hairy leukoplakia earlier, Pneumocystis pneumonia below 200, Toxoplasma encephalitis below 100, and CMV retinitis and Mycobacterium avium complex below 50.

Relate noninfectious AIDS complications to their causes: Kaposi sarcoma (HHV-8), primary CNS lymphoma (EBV), HIV-associated nephropathy (collapsing FSGS), neurocognitive disorder, peripheral neuropathy, and immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome.

IM-15-C.t: Explain type I hypersensitivity: Th2 and IL-4 driven IgE sensitization, mast cell FcepsilonRI cross-linking on re-exposure, immediate histamine and tryptase release, and a late phase of leukotrienes and eosinophils.
IM-15-C.usmle: Immune System: Immunologically mediated disorders: hypersensitivity

IM-15-C.t: Identify anaphylaxis from common triggers (foods such as peanut, insect stings, penicillin, latex) by urticaria, angioedema, bronchospasm, and hypotension, and interpret an elevated serum tryptase.
IM-15-C.usmle: Immune System: Immunologically mediated disorders: hypersensitivity: anaphylaxis

IM-15-C.t: Compare warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia (IgG, extravascular splenic hemolysis, spherocytes; SLE, CLL) with cold agglutinin disease (IgM fixing complement; Mycoplasma pneumoniae, EBV; acrocyanosis), both with positive direct Coombs test.
IM-15-C.usmle: Immune System: Immunologically mediated disorders: hypersensitivity

IM-15-C.t: Explain Goodpasture syndrome (anti-GBM disease; antibodies to the alpha3 chain of type IV collagen) causing hemoptysis and rapidly progressive crescentic glomerulonephritis with linear IgG on immunofluorescence.
IM-15-C.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: immunologic and inflammatory disorders: Goodpasture syndrome

IM-15-C.t: Explain myasthenia gravis as noncytotoxic type II hypersensitivity (antibodies to the acetylcholine receptor or MuSK), with fatigable ptosis, diplopia, and proximal weakness, and its association with thymic hyperplasia and thymoma.
IM-15-C.usmle: Immune System: Immunologically mediated disorders: hypersensitivity

IM-15-C.t: Explain SLE pathogenesis (impaired clearance of apoptotic nuclear material, immune complexes) and interpret ANA (sensitive), anti-dsDNA and anti-Smith (specific), anti-histone (drug-induced), and low C3 and C4 during flares.
IM-15-C.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: immunologic and inflammatory disorders: systemic lupus erythematosus

IM-15-C.t: Identify SLE manifestations in a young woman (malar rash, photosensitivity, nonerosive arthritis, serositis, cytopenias, lupus nephritis with wire loops, Libman-Sacks endocarditis) and antiphospholipid syndrome thrombosis and pregnancy loss.
IM-15-C.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: immunologic and inflammatory disorders: systemic lupus erythematosus

IM-15-C.t: Describe polyarteritis nodosa: immune complex medium-vessel vasculitis linked to hepatitis B, ANCA-negative, sparing the lungs, with transmural fibrinoid necrosis at different stages and renal and mesenteric microaneurysms.
IM-15-C.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: immunologic and inflammatory disorders: polyarteritis nodosa

IM-15-C.t: Explain poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis 1 to 4 weeks after group A strep pharyngitis or skin infection: nephritic syndrome, low C3, elevated ASO or anti-DNase B, subepithelial humps, and granular immunofluorescence.
IM-15-C.usmle: Immune System: Immunologically mediated disorders: hypersensitivity

IM-15-C.t: Describe rheumatoid arthritis pathogenesis (HLA-DR4, citrullinated peptide autoimmunity, synovial pannus) and findings: symmetric MCP, PIP, and wrist erosions sparing DIP joints, rheumatoid factor, anti-CCP, nodules, and Felty syndrome.
IM-15-C.usmle: Immune System: Immunologically mediated disorders: hypersensitivity

IM-15-C.t: Explain type IV granulomatous inflammation (Th1 IFN-gamma activating macrophages, TNF maintaining granulomas), distinguishing caseating tuberculosis granulomas from noncaseating ones, and interpret a tuberculin skin test read at 48 to 72 hours.
IM-15-C.usmle: Immune System: Immunologically mediated disorders: hypersensitivity: type 4

IM-15-C.t: Identify sarcoidosis by noncaseating granulomas, bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, elevated ACE, hypercalcemia, uveitis, and erythema nodosum, and recognize Lofgren syndrome (erythema nodosum, hilar adenopathy, arthritis).
IM-15-C.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: immunologic and inflammatory disorders: sarcoidosis, Lofgren syndrome

IM-15-C.t: Compare hyperacute (preformed antibody, minutes), acute (T cell or antibody mediated, weeks to months), and chronic (graft arteriosclerosis, bronchiolitis obliterans, months to years) rejection, and distinguish graft-versus-host disease (skin, liver, gut).
IM-15-C.usmle: Immune System: Immunologically mediated disorders: transplantation

IM-15-C.t: Explain serum sickness (fever, urticaria, arthralgia, proteinuria, low complement about 1 to 2 weeks after foreign protein exposure) and the local Arthus reaction as systemic and local type III reactions.
IM-15-C.usmle: Immune System: Immunologically mediated disorders: hypersensitivity: serum sickness

IM-15-C.t: Classify drug hypersensitivity examples by mechanism: penicillin anaphylaxis (type I), penicillin or methyldopa hemolytic anemia (type II), serum sickness from chimeric antibodies (type III), and contact dermatitis from topical neomycin (type IV).
IM-15-C.usmle: Immune System: Immunologically mediated disorders: hypersensitivity: drug reactions

IM-15-D.t: Explain systemic sclerosis pathogenesis (endothelial injury, autoimmunity, TGF-beta driven fibroblast collagen deposition) causing skin thickening, Raynaud phenomenon, esophageal dysmotility, and interstitial lung disease.
IM-15-D.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: immunologic and inflammatory disorders: scleroderma (systemic sclerosis)

IM-15-D.t: Distinguish diffuse systemic sclerosis (anti-Scl-70, early visceral disease, scleroderma renal crisis) from limited CREST disease (anticentromere; calcinosis, Raynaud, esophageal dysmotility, sclerodactyly, telangiectasia; pulmonary hypertension).
IM-15-D.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: immunologic and inflammatory disorders: scleroderma (systemic sclerosis)

IM-15-D.t: Explain acute rheumatic fever as type II hypersensitivity from M protein mimicry of cardiac proteins 2 to 4 weeks after untreated group A strep pharyngitis, with Aschoff bodies and Anitschkow cells in pancarditis.
IM-15-D.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: immunologic and inflammatory disorders: acute rheumatic fever

IM-15-D.t: Apply the Jones major criteria (migratory polyarthritis, carditis, subcutaneous nodules, erythema marginatum, Sydenham chorea) with evidence of strep infection, and predict chronic mitral stenosis.
IM-15-D.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: immunologic and inflammatory disorders: acute rheumatic fever

IM-15-D.t: Explain Sjogren syndrome (lymphocytic destruction of salivary and lacrimal glands) causing dry mouth and keratoconjunctivitis sicca, with anti-Ro (SSA) and anti-La (SSB), RA association, and marginal zone lymphoma risk.
IM-15-D.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: immunologic and inflammatory disorders: Sjogren syndrome

IM-15-D.t: Predict congenital heart block and neonatal lupus in infants of mothers with anti-Ro (SSA) antibodies from Sjogren syndrome or SLE, through transplacental IgG.
IM-15-D.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: immunologic and inflammatory disorders: Sjogren syndrome

IM-15-D.t: Identify mixed connective tissue disease by overlapping features of SLE, systemic sclerosis, and polymyositis with high-titer anti-U1 RNP antibodies.
IM-15-D.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: immunologic and inflammatory disorders: mixed connective tissue disease

IM-15-E.t: Describe amyloid as misfolded proteins in beta-pleated sheets deposited extracellularly, showing apple-green birefringence with Congo red under polarized light, and diagnosed by abdominal fat pad or organ biopsy.
IM-15-E.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Genetic, metabolic, and developmental disorders: amyloidosis

IM-15-E.t: Explain primary (AL) amyloidosis from monoclonal plasma cell light chains (a plasma cell dyscrasia, sometimes with multiple myeloma) and predict restrictive cardiomyopathy, nephrotic syndrome, macroglossia, periorbital purpura, and carpal tunnel neuropathy.
IM-15-E.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Genetic, metabolic, and developmental disorders: amyloidosis

IM-15-E.t: Explain secondary (AA) amyloidosis from serum amyloid A in chronic inflammation (rheumatoid arthritis, inflammatory bowel disease, chronic infections, familial Mediterranean fever) and predict renal involvement with nephrotic syndrome.
IM-15-E.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: immunologic and inflammatory disorders: familial Mediterranean fever

IM-15-E.t: Match other amyloid proteins to their settings: beta2-microglobulin (long-term dialysis), transthyretin (wild-type age-related cardiac and hereditary), A-beta (Alzheimer disease), calcitonin (medullary thyroid carcinoma), and amylin (type 2 diabetes islets).
IM-15-E.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Genetic, metabolic, and developmental disorders: amyloidosis

IM-15-F.t: Identify erythema infectiosum (slapped cheek then lacy reticular rash in children, arthropathy in adults) and predict parvovirus B19 aplastic crisis in hemolytic anemias and hydrops fetalis in pregnancy.
IM-15-F.usmle: Skin & Subcutaneous Tissue: Infectious disorders and infestations: viral: erythema infectiosum (fifth disease)

IM-15-F.t: Identify invasive Haemophilus influenzae type b disease in unvaccinated young children (epiglottitis with drooling and stridor, meningitis, bacteremia, pneumonia), and contrast nontypeable strains causing otitis media and sinusitis.
IM-15-F.usmle: Respiratory System: Infectious disorders of the upper airways: epiglottitis

IM-15-F.t: Identify influenza by abrupt fever, myalgia, headache, and cough, and predict complications: primary viral pneumonia, secondary bacterial pneumonia (S aureus, S pneumoniae), and Reye syndrome with aspirin use in children.
IM-15-F.usmle: Respiratory System: Infectious disorders of the upper airways: viral infections: influenza virus

IM-15-F.t: Identify measles by cough, coryza, conjunctivitis, Koplik spots, and a rash spreading from the head downward, and predict pneumonia, encephalitis, subacute sclerosing panencephalitis, and worse outcomes with vitamin A deficiency.
IM-15-F.usmle: Skin & Subcutaneous Tissue: Infectious disorders and infestations: viral: measles

IM-15-F.t: Identify infectious mononucleosis in an adolescent (fever, pharyngitis, posterior cervical lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly) by atypical CD8 T lymphocytes and heterophile antibodies, and predict rash after amoxicillin.
IM-15-F.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: viral infections: infectious mononucleosis (Epstein-Barr virus)

IM-15-F.t: Predict complications of EBV infection: splenic rupture, hepatitis, autoimmune hemolytic anemia, and associated malignancies (Burkitt lymphoma, Hodgkin lymphoma, nasopharyngeal carcinoma, lymphoma in immunosuppression).
IM-15-F.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: viral infections: infectious mononucleosis (Epstein-Barr virus)

IM-15-F.t: Identify mumps by parotitis, and predict orchitis in postpubertal males, aseptic meningitis, and pancreatitis, with elevated serum amylase.
IM-15-F.usmle: Gastrointestinal System: Infectious disorders: viral: mumps

IM-15-F.t: Identify roseola infantum (HHV-6, less often HHV-7) in a child under 2 years: several days of high fever, then a truncal rash as the fever breaks, with risk of febrile seizures.
IM-15-F.usmle: Skin & Subcutaneous Tissue: Infectious disorders and infestations: viral: roseola (exanthema subitum)

IM-15-F.t: Identify rubella (enveloped positive-sense RNA virus) by mild face-to-trunk rash, postauricular lymphadenopathy, and adult arthralgia, and predict congenital rubella (cataracts, sensorineural deafness, PDA, blueberry muffin rash) after first trimester infection.
IM-15-F.usmle: Skin & Subcutaneous Tissue: Infectious disorders and infestations: viral: rubella

IM-15-F.t: Identify scarlet fever after strep pharyngitis (sandpaper rash, circumoral pallor, strawberry tongue, Pastia lines, later desquamation) and predict rheumatic fever and poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis.
IM-15-F.usmle: Skin & Subcutaneous Tissue: Infectious disorders and infestations: bacterial: scarlet fever (group A Streptococcus)

IM-15-F.t: Predict toxoplasmosis presentations: mono-like lymphadenopathy in healthy hosts, congenital chorioretinitis, hydrocephalus, and diffuse intracranial calcifications, and multiple ring-enhancing brain lesions in AIDS with CD4 below 100.
IM-15-F.usmle: Nervous System & Special Senses: Infectious disorders: encephalitis: Toxoplasma gondii

IM-15-F.t: Distinguish the childhood exanthems by rash pattern and timing relative to fever: measles, rubella, erythema infectiosum, roseola, and scarlet fever.
IM-15-F.usmle: Skin & Subcutaneous Tissue: Infectious disorders and infestations: viral: erythema infectiosum, rubella, measles, roseola

IM-15-F.t: Identify CMV infection: heterophile-negative mononucleosis, owl's eye inclusions, congenital infection with periventricular calcifications and hearing loss, and retinitis, colitis, or pneumonitis in transplant and AIDS patients.
IM-15-F.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: viral infections: cytomegalovirus infection
